features.summary: Recent changes in the libwebrtc build process focus on improving how the code is managed and integrated. Updates to scripts like `vendor-libwebrtc.py` allow it to be called from other Python programs, which enhances flexibility for developers when working with WebRTC, the technology behind video calls. Additionally, renaming and adjusting the scope of certain variables aims to streamline the build process, making it easier to manage local vendoring of the WebRTC library. These enhancements, including a new Python-based version of a build script, are critical for ensuring faster and more efficient development, contributing to overall performance improvements in Firefox. **Users will benefit indirectly from this smoother development workflow as it can lead to quicker updates and features in their browser.**

features.summary: Common WebRTC plumbing improved: Firefox now fully supports extmap-allow-mixed (an RTP/RTCP header extension rule that allows mixing one-byte and two-byte extension formats), which makes header-extension handling more standards-compliant. The WebRTC port allowlist was exposed as a shared helper so different parts of the code use the same policy, and a small off-by-one bug in video stamping was fixed. Together these changes improve interoperability and internal correctness.

features.label: Negotiation engine (JSEP)

patches.author: Nicolas Grunbaum
patches.subject: Add distinct errors for SDP parsing failures.

patches.author: Sylvestre Ledru
patches.subject: Apply std::move in dom (assorted modules) where values can be moved instead of copied

features.summary: Recent updates to the negotiation engine in Firefox's JSEP (JavaScript Session Establishment Protocol) have improved how the browser handles errors related to SDP (Session Description Protocol) parsing. By introducing distinct error messages for parsing failures, developers can more easily identify and troubleshoot issues that arise during the establishment of multimedia sessions, such as video calls through WebRTC (the technology behind video calls). Additionally, applying `std::move` in various parts of the browser's code enhances performance by allowing the efficient transfer of data rather than duplicating it, leading to a smoother user experience without apparent _visible change_.

features.label: WebRTC

patches.author: Byron Campen
patches.subject: Implement RTCTransportStats.selectedCandidatePairChanges

patches.author: Chun-Min Chang
patches.subject: Return nsresult from AudioPacketizer::Input and guard sample-count calculation

features.summary: Recent updates to WebRTC, the technology behind video calls, include the addition of **RTCTransportStats.selectedCandidatePairChanges**. This feature enhances the ability to track changes in the network paths used for media streams, providing better insights into connection quality and optimization. Additionally, an improvement was made in audio processing with the introduction of an error handling mechanism in AudioPacketizer, which helps ensure more reliable audio playback by accurately calculating sample counts. These enhancements contribute to a smoother and more efficient user experience during video calls and streaming.

features.label: Session negotiation (SDP)

patches.author: Byron Campen
patches.subject: Fix a latent off-by-one bug.

features.summary: Recent updates in the session negotiation area of Firefox have addressed a latent off-by-one bug in the Session Description Protocol (SDP), which is crucial for managing media sessions in technologies like WebRTC, the backbone of video calling and real-time communication. Fixing this bug helps ensure that media data is handled more accurately during negotiations, leading to a more reliable and efficient connection setup. While users may not notice any immediate changes, this fix contributes to smoother performance and stability in applications that rely on real-time media.
